title: Greatest musical experiences and a playgoing couple
summary: Moore names Armstrong then Bechet as his peak, and he and Ida attend plays.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well, Russell, what would you say has been perhaps the most thrilling and satisfying musical experience you've had in your long career? If you could pick out one musical experience, what would that be?

Well, you can't -- I can't just right now off the bat say, this is my greatest, because I've had some great moments and most of the -- wherever I appear. I think being with Armstrong is one of the greatest moments in a long stretch. Even with the big band in the '40s, I think being with Louie is one of the great experiences.

The next one would be with Sidney Bechet. Because I could not learn quite a bit off of them people. And I/project what experience I've had with those two men, like Sidney and Louie. Also many of the musicians around the City of New York. I love to go in to sit and hear different people. I intend to go down and hear Eubie Blake and I want to go again to hear Alberta Hunter. And any time the Preservation bands come from New Orleans to Rockland County, they always play the Rockland County College, I go to hear them. Or any of the plays that they have at West Point, we used to go to

West Point to see a play. That is to say that my wife, Ida, and I are playgoers. We have seen "Aint Misbehaving" and most all the musicals that come through, from "Fair Lady" on down, and always take friends with us that like plays -- "Fiddler on the Roof." Just different plays. In that way we love New York although we're not in New York proper, we love Nyack, of course. We bought this home here, it's a custom-built house and it's just nice.
